These are current dependency and boundary-scope defects; neither is a counterexample to the recomputed certificate inequalities.

Enumeration of the generator's 159 distinct component argument intervals confirmed positive cosine denominators, atan arguments above 1, positive square-root inputs and supported trigonometric radii. The universal enclosure arguments were checked analytically, including interior extrema, terminating atan reductions and derivative hypotheses. Normal and -O executions each passed all eight certificate tests and 22 interval tests. Table regeneration in both modes exactly matched the frozen table, which is embedded verbatim in the supplied document. Independently executed valid-interface controls confirmed generator exits 1/2/1 for false/exception/unknown results, receiver rejection, preservation of previous publication bytes and rejection of an altered contract. However, the frozen test's own receiver negative controls never exercise reception: they pass unsupported --ledger and obtain argparse exit 2 even for the valid certificate. That remaining regression/evidence defect requires correction; no failed mathematical certificate was found.
